apart.note: Lewis & Short s.v. prodigium: "for prodicium, from prodico"; s.v. prodigus: [prodigo].
Lewis & Short s.v. mansio: [maneo], a staying; mandō, mandere, to chew, only shares the stem of its participle.
Lewis & Short s.v. conus: Greek κῶνος, a cone; cōnor is to try.

Lewis & Short s.v. specus: “perh. root spec-”; de Vaan s.v. speciō: specus “is usually derived from *spek- ‘to see’, but the semantics do not impose this view”. Too doubtful to join a cave with a look-out.
Lewis & Short s.v. schedius: schedia is Greek σχεδία, a raft; scheda (s.v. scida) is a leaf of paper.
Neither Lewis & Short nor de Vaan has Austria; no derivation from auster, the south wind, was found, so the two are not joined.
Lewis & Short s.v. sarculum: [sario = sarrio], to hoe; not sarcio, to mend.
Lewis & Short gives no derivation; de Vaan s.v. surus, a stake, has surculus as its derivative and sura only with a query.
Lewis & Short s.v. emendo: [mendum]; commendo is the compound of mando.
The Albanian is not named from the Elbe; Lewis & Short s.v. Albanus: [Alba].
Lewis & Short s.v. rogus gives no derivation from rogo; de Vaan has rogus, funeral pyre, under rego.
Lewis & Short s.v. hortor: "for horitor, v. horior"; hortus is the garden.
Lewis & Short s.v. articulus: dim. [2. artus], a joint.
Lewis & Short s.v. sentis, a thorn-bush, gives no derivation from sentio.
Lewis & Short s.v. bellaria, dessert, gives no derivation; none from bellum, war, was found.
Lewis & Short s.v. bubulo: [bubo], the owl; bubula is beef.
Lewis & Short s.v. calamitas: "cf. incolumis"; calamus is the reed.
Lewis & Short s.v. campana, a bell (late Latin), gives no derivation from campus.
Lewis & Short s.v. carpinus, hornbeam, gives no derivation; carpus is the wrist.
Lewis & Short s.v. castro: "Sanscr. çastra, knife"; castra is the camp.
Lewis & Short s.v. concilium: "con- and root cal- of calo"; cilium is the eyelid.
Lewis & Short s.v. ventus: "Sanscr. vā, blow"; not the participle of venio.
Lewis & Short s.v. mutus: "root mu-, to shut"; muto is to change.
Lewis & Short s.v. cremum: "= cremor", broth; cremo is to burn.
crocia, a crosier (the stick of lacrosse), is not in Lewis & Short and no derivation from crocus, saffron, was found.
cubus is Greek κύβος, a cube; Lewis & Short s.v. cubo names no noun as its source.
Lewis & Short s.v. cubile: [cubo].
Lewis & Short s.v. cubiculum: [cubo].
Lewis & Short: colon is Greek κῶλον, the gut; 1. colum is a strainer.
Lewis & Short s.v. fatuus: "root fa, cf. for".
Lewis & Short s.v. curia: "kindr. with Quiris, Quirites".
Lewis & Short s.v. curiosus: [cura].
Lewis & Short s.v. incuria: [2. in-cura].
Lewis & Short has salio, to salt, from sal, and salio, to leap, apart from it; the lexicon has the second.
As for sāl: Lewis & Short keeps salio, to leap, apart from sal.
Lewis & Short s.v. dolo, to hew: "cf. Sanscr. dar-, dal-, to tear apart"; dolus is a trick.
Lewis & Short s.v. delibero: "de and libro, libra"; not from liber, free.
Lewis & Short: de-mens, out of one's mind (mens); demo is to take away.
Lewis & Short s.v. expers: [pars]; inexpertus is in- with expertus, from experior.
Lewis & Short s.v. exsilium: [exsul]; exsilio is to leap out.
Lewis & Short s.v. spira: "= σπεῖρα", a coil; s.v. spiro: "etym. dub.".
Lewis & Short s.v. externus: [exter].
Lewis & Short s.v. internus: "in; cf. interior, intestinus, intus".
Lewis & Short s.v. famulus: "Osc. faama, house"; fames is hunger.
Lewis & Short s.v. fello, to suck, gives no derivation from fel, gall.
Lewis & Short s.v. fere: "Sanscr. dhar-, to bear, support; Lat. firmus"; not the adverb of ferus.
Lewis & Short s.v. ferio says only "perh. … Lat. ferus, ferox": too doubtful to join.
As for ferus.
Lewis & Short s.v. ferula, the fennel-giant, gives no derivation from fera.
As for fera.
Lewis & Short s.v. fidelia, an earthen pot, gives no derivation from fidelis.
Lewis & Short s.v. felio: the cry of the male panther; no derivation from feles is given.
Lewis & Short s.v. filia: [filius]; filum is a thread.
Lewis & Short s.v. gloria: "Sanscr. cru, to hear … Lat. cluo"; glos is a sister-in-law.
Lewis & Short s.v. pergula: [pergo; cf. tegula, from tego].
Lewis & Short s.v. nato: freq. of [no], to swim; nates are the buttocks.
Lewis & Short s.v. viduus: "Sanscr. vidhava, without a husband".
As for videō.
Lewis & Short s.v. medium: "v. medius"; medius is "Sanscr. madhya", not from medeor.
Lewis & Short s.v. remedium: [re-medeor].
Lewis & Short s.v. merula, a blackbird, gives no derivation from merus.
Lewis & Short s.v. mortarium, a mortar, gives no derivation from mors.
Lewis & Short s.v. mulsum: "v. mulceo, P. a."; mulgeo is to milk.
Lewis & Short s.v. Palatium: the hill, "root pa-, to protect"; palatum is the palate.
Lewis & Short s.v. perpetuus: [peto].
Lewis & Short derives both from praehendo, but praedium, an estate, is not made from praeda, booty; they are left apart.
Lewis & Short s.v. pulto: "collat. form of pulso, from pello"; puls is porridge.
Lewis & Short s.v. sepia: "= σηπία", the cuttlefish; saepes is a hedge.
Lewis & Short: scopulus is Greek σκόπελος, a rock; scopus is σκοπός, a target.
Lewis & Short s.v. speculum: [specio]; specus is a cave.
Lewis & Short s.v. stipula: dim. [stipes]; stips is a small coin.
Lewis & Short s.v. sudarium: [sudor]; sudus, dry, is [se-udus].
Lewis & Short s.v. taedium: [taedet]; s.v. taeda, pine torch: "etym. dub.".
Lewis & Short s.v. taxo: freq. of [tago, tango]; taxus is the yew.
Lewis & Short s.v. terrifico: [terrificus], from terreo.
Lewis & Short: tonus is Greek τόνος; tono, to thunder, is not made from it.
Lewis & Short s.v. uncia: "= οὐγκία … akin to unus"; uncus is a hook.
As for vaccīnum.
Lewis & Short s.v. vaccinium: the blueberry; the vaccine (vaccīnum, from vacca) is another word.
Lewis & Short s.v. violo: [vis]; viola is the violet.
Lewis & Short s.v. venalis: [2. venus], sale; vena is a vein.
Lewis & Short s.v. venor, to hunt, gives no derivation from vena.
Lewis & Short: e-mineo, to stand out (cf. s.v. immineo: [in-mineo]); not a compound of maneo.
Lewis & Short s.v. immineo: [in-mineo].
Lewis & Short s.v. insector: freq. of [insequor]; insectum is "v. 1. inseco".
Lewis & Short s.v. solidus: "old Lat. sollus"; de Vaan s.v. solidus: a derivation from soleo is unlikely.
Lewis & Short has lātus, wide ("old Lat. stlātus"), apart from lātus, the participle of fero.
Lewis & Short s.v. 2. impropero, to reproach: "corrupt. for improbro; from in-probrum".
Lewis & Short s.v. pilo: [1. pilus], a hair; pila is a ball.
Lewis & Short has luxus, dislocated, with luxo, and luxus, luxury ("root luc-"), apart; the lexicon has the second.
Lewis & Short s.v. germen: "Sanscr. root grabh-, to conceive"; not from gero.
Lewis & Short s.v. salvia, sage, gives no derivation; unverified, so not joined.
Lewis & Short s.v. Olympia: the Greek name of the place in Elis; no derivation from the mountain is given.
Lewis & Short s.v. 1. comparo, to compare: [compar]; only 2. comparo, to prepare, is from paro.
Lewis & Short has 1. paro, to prepare ("cf. pario"), apart from 2. paro, to make equal, [par].
As for the noun.
As for the noun.
Lewis & Short s.v. servus: "referred by the ancients to servo", which it does not adopt; s.v. servo: "cf. salus".
Lewis & Short s.v. operio: [pario; cf. aperio]; not from opus or opera.
As for opera.
Lewis & Short has pullus, a young animal ("root pu-, to beget"), and pullus, dark ("kindr. with πελλός"), as two words.
Lewis & Short gives no derivation for mundus, the world; de Vaan has the two words in separate articles.
Lewis & Short s.v. altaria offers two derivations, "cf. adoleo … or altus from its height": undecided, so not joined.
Lewis & Short s.v. aureus: [aurum].
Lewis & Short s.v. aureus: [aurum].
Lewis & Short s.v. auricula: [auris].
Lewis & Short s.v. auricula: [auris].
Lewis & Short s.v. gallina: [1. gallus].
Lewis & Short s.v. mentalis: [mens].
Lewis & Short s.v. mentalis: [mens].
Lewis & Short s.v. moralis: [mores].
Lewis & Short s.v. generalis: [genus].
Lewis & Short s.v. generosus: [genus].
Lewis & Short s.v. mensarius: [mensa].
Lewis & Short s.v. vinculum: [vincio], to bind; not from vinco.
Lewis & Short s.v. jaculum: [jaculus], the adjective of jacio, to throw; not from jaceo.
Lewis & Short s.v. curriculum: [curro].
Lewis & Short s.v. testiculus: dim. [2. testis].
Lewis & Short s.v. testiculus: dim. [2. testis]; the witness is 1. testis.
Lewis & Short s.v. testor: [1. testis].
Lewis & Short s.v. collare: [collum].
Lewis & Short s.v. tentorium: [tendo].
Lewis & Short s.v. terricula: [terreo].
Lewis & Short s.v. morosus: [mos].
Lewis & Short s.v. morigerus: [mos-gero].
Lewis & Short s.v. forensis: [forum].
Lewis & Short s.v. forensis: [forum].
Lewis & Short s.v. pallium: "cf. palla".
Lewis & Short s.v. muscosus: [muscus], moss.
Lewis & Short s.v. clavicula: dim. [clavis].
Lewis & Short s.v. clavicula: dim. [clavis].
The verbal noun of hortor (Lewis & Short s.v. hortor), not made from hortus.
The verbal noun of venor, to hunt; not made from vena.
The participle of paro (Lewis & Short s.v. 1. paro), not made from par.
As for the neuter noun.
The participle of effero (Lewis & Short s.v. lātus: "Part., v. fero"), not a compound of lātus, wide.
The participle of transfero, as ēlātus is of effero.
Lewis & Short: co-hortor, the compound of hortor.
Lewis & Short: re-sto, the compound of sto; restis is a rope.
Lewis & Short: red-oleo, the compound of oleo.
Lewis & Short: prae-dico, the compound of dico.
Lewis & Short s.v. conversio: [converto].
Lewis & Short s.v. decretum: "v. decerno fin."
Lewis & Short s.v. commentum: "v. comminiscor fin."
Lewis & Short s.v. versus, a line: [verto].
Lewis & Short s.v. bonitas: [bonus].
Lewis & Short s.v. proprietas: [proprius].
Lewis & Short s.v. veritas: [verus].
Lewis & Short s.v. particula: dim. [pars].
Lewis & Short s.v. labo: "from the same root as 1. labor"; it gives no derivation for labium, the lip. Nothing joins them.
Lewis & Short s.v. hostia: [2. hostio, acc. to Paul. ex Fest.]; hostis is another word.
Lewis & Short s.v. munio: [moenia, lit. to wall]; s.v. munia: that to which one is bound, with munus and immunis. The duties and the walls are kept apart.
The lexicon's sector is the deponent verb, to follow eagerly (Lewis & Short 2. sector, freq. of sequor), not 1. sector, a cutter [seco].
As sector and secō: the verb sector is from sequor; sectiō is from secō.
Lewis & Short s.v. intibus (also intubus): from Greek ἔντυβον, endive; not in- before tubus, a pipe (Lewis & Short s.v. tubus).

together.note: Lewis & Short s.v. inimicus: [2. in-amicus]. The weakened vowel hides it from the method.
Lewis & Short s.v. mansio: [maneo]. The participle of mandō, to chew, has the same stem.
Lewis & Short s.v. 1. specula and s.v. speculum: both [specio]; de Vaan s.v. speciō has speculum.
Lewis & Short s.v. ineptus: [2. in-aptus].
Lewis & Short s.v. iniquus: [2. in-aequus].
Lewis & Short s.v. 2. liber, liberi, children: [1. liber].
Lewis & Short s.v. curiosus: [cura]; s.v. incuria: [2. in-cura].
Lewis & Short s.v. cubile: [cubo].
Lewis & Short s.v. remedium: [re-medeor].
Lewis & Short s.v. absens: "Part. of absum".
Lewis & Short s.v. praesens: "v. praesum fin."
Lewis & Short s.v. potens: "P. a., v. possum fin."; s.v. possibilis: [possum].
Lewis & Short s.v. nolo: [ne-volo]; s.v. malo: [magis-volo]; s.v. voluntas: [1. volo].
Lewis & Short s.v. fio: "v. facio init.": fio serves as its passive.
Lewis & Short s.v. iter: "for itiner, from īre, ĭtum".
Lewis & Short s.v. sciens: "Part. and P. a., from scio"; s.v. scientia: [sciens]; ne-scio.

Lewis & Short s.v. 1. do names its compounds "edere, tradere, dedere; reddere"; s.v. trado: [trans-do]; s.v. vendo: "contr. from venum-do". Compounds of the third conjugation, which the method does not join to dare.
Lewis & Short s.v. calco: [1. calx], the heel.
Lewis & Short s.v. calculus: dim. [2. calx], limestone; s.v. calcarius: [2. calx].
Lewis & Short s.v. juro: [2. jus], law; s.v. justus: [2. jus].
Lewis & Short s.v. jusculum: dim. [1. jus], broth.
Lewis & Short s.v. apium: [apis]; s.v. apiarius: [apis]. The root ap- is too short for the method.
Lewis & Short s.v. opera: [opus].
Lewis & Short s.v. viso: freq. of [video].
Lewis & Short s.v. filia: [filius].
Lewis & Short s.v. domina: [dominus].
Lewis & Short s.v. vērum: "v. verus".
Lewis & Short s.v. diva: "a goddess, v. divus".
Lewis & Short s.v. irascor: [ira].
Lewis & Short s.v. spinus: [spina].
Lewis & Short s.v. pedum, a shepherd's crook: [pes].
Lewis & Short s.v. vinculum: [vincio].

de Vaan s.v. plūs lists plūrēs, plūrimus, plūrālis, and complūrēs as its derivatives; Lewis & Short s.v. multus: "Comp.: plūs, plūris; in the plur., plūres, plūra", s.v. pluralis: [plus], s.v. complures: com-plūres.

homographs.note: Lewis & Short has 1. jus, broth, and 2. jus, law, with the same forms.
Lewis & Short has 2. malus, an apple-tree, and 3. malus, a mast.
Lewis & Short has 1. calx, the heel, and 2. calx, limestone (and the goal marked with it).
